Simulate an illustrative count-outcome dataset

Source: R/simulate_count.R
simulate_count.Rd

Generate fully synthetic data for demonstrating count treatment-effect methods. Treatment is assigned by a logistic treatment model. Relapse counts follow a Poisson or negative binomial distribution with a log-rate model, treatment interactions and varying follow-up. Coefficients are illustrative, not clinical estimates or a reconstruction of the MarketScan data.

Usage

simulate_count(
  n = 4000L,
  seed = 20261114L,
  ps_weights = c(intercept = 0.11, age = 1.15, drugB = 0.25, drugC = -0.2),
  lp_weights = c(intercept = log(0.5), age = 0.25, female = 0.12, previous_cost = 0.1,
    previous_number_relapses = 0.16, treatment_age = -0.2, treatment_relapses = -0.12),
  conditional_rr = 0.9,
  followup_range = c(0.5, 3),
  dispersion = Inf
)

Arguments

n

Positive integer sample size. Default is 4,000.

seed

Integer seed, or NULL to use the current random-number state. Supplying a seed sets R's random-number state.

ps_weights

Named coefficients for treatment assignment. Recognized names are intercept, age, drugB, and drugC; named subsets override the defaults. Age is measured in decades from 48 years, and drugA is the reference previous treatment.

lp_weights

Named coefficients for the log relapse rate. Recognized names are intercept, age, female, previous_cost, previous_number_relapses, treatment_age, and treatment_relapses; named subsets override the defaults. Age is measured in decades from 48 years and cost is centered at 13,824 and divided by 20,172 US dollars. The intercept is the log annual rate under drug0 at the reference covariate values.

conditional_rr

Positive rate ratio for drug1 versus drug0 at age 48 and zero previous relapses. Elsewhere its log is log(conditional_rr) + treatment_age * (age_in_years - 48)/10 + treatment_relapses * previous_number_relapses.

followup_range

Two finite positive values specifying the minimum and maximum follow-up in years. Follow-up is sampled uniformly and independently of covariates, treatment and the outcome process; equal values give constant follow-up.

dispersion

Positive negative-binomial size parameter, or Inf (the default) for Poisson counts. For finite size, the count variance is mean + mean^2 / dispersion.

Value

A data frame with centered age, female, previous_treatment, scaled previous_cost, previous_number_symptoms, previous_number_relapses, trt, count outcome y, and follow-up in years years. Age and cost retain centering and scaling attributes. Treatment labels are drug0 and drug1.

Details

The model assumes a constant individual event rate over follow-up; conditional on covariates, treatment and follow-up, expected counts equal the annual rate multiplied by follow-up. Extreme coefficients may cause poor overlap or invalid rates. The generator is for illustration, not a calibrated representation of any patient population.

Author

Thomas Debray tdebray@fromdatatowisdom.com

Examples

toy <- simulate_count(n = 500, seed = 1)
table(toy$trt)
#> 
#> drug0 drug1 
#>   224   276 
toy_overdispersed <- simulate_count(n = 500, seed = 1,
  conditional_rr = 0.8, dispersion = 2)
